title: One rule for unplaceable references, and evidence-aware severity
summary: This change replaces six overlapping reference rules (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start) with a single `unplaceable-reference` rule backed by a new candidate engine in `crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs`. The engine finds four kinds of unresolvable reference — numbers, phrases, times and names — and decides per candidate whether the surrounding paragraph places it. Alongside it, `osf-lint-core`'s `resolve` gains an `Evidence` argument: a finding backed only by statistical evidence (a guessed name, a quoted term, a developer tool) always resolves to a warning that advises, in every context, so a weak guess can never refuse a reply. A 98-fixture corpus and a precision/recall measure pin the new rule's behaviour, and end-to-end tests prove it fires at the stop hook, the commit-message check and the prompt hook.

lanes.label: Entry points
lanes.subtitle: hooks, CLI, scan
lanes.summary: The surfaces that hand text to the writing lint: the stop hook, the commit-message check, the prompt hook and the scan command.

lanes.label: Writing lint
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints
lanes.summary: The rule pipeline that turns a document into findings, including the new candidate engine and the placement decision.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared severity resolution: class, group, context, exception and now evidence decide a finding's level and remediation.

lanes.label: Fixtures and measures
lanes.subtitle: tests
lanes.summary: The 98-file unplaceable corpus, the precision/recall measure and the end-to-end checkpoint tests that hold the new rule to its contract.

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: hook.rs stop_with_input
nodes.summary: Reads the assistant's last message from stdin and refuses the turn when a blocking finding is present. A new test proves a reply whose only finding is a weak-evidence name is not refused.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: verify.rs pre-commit
nodes.summary: Lints the commit message file in commit context. Its expected error count moves from one to two because the old chat-local rule and the new rule both fire until the old one is retired.

nodes.label: Prompt hook
nodes.subtitle: hook prompt
nodes.summary: Prints the reminder shown on every prompt. A new test asserts it never names one of the six retired rule ids.

nodes.label: Scan command
nodes.subtitle: scan/mod.rs resolve_and_explain
nodes.summary: Resolves each finding's level and remediation from its rule metadata; now passes the finding's own evidence through to the core resolver.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: The writing pipeline. It now calls the new unplaceable_reference rule after undefined_names, and apply_context passes evidence through for the new rule while older rules keep deterministic resolution.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: The new rule. It gathers candidates per paragraph, keeps the first use of each name, picks one paragraph to report a repeated name from, and emits a finding for every candidate the paragraph does not place.

nodes.label: Candidate engine
nodes.subtitle: reference.rs candidates()
nodes.summary: Finds number, phrase, time and name candidates in a paragraph. It masks quoted and backticked spans, keeps the longest candidate per kind on overlap, and gathers multi-word name-repeat counts across the whole document.

nodes.label: Placement decision
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs is_placed
nodes.summary: Decides whether a candidate is resolved by its paragraph: a link, a bracketed or colon description, a repository or file name, an absolute date, a known name, a definer sentence or a mention marker.

nodes.label: Rule metadata
nodes.subtitle: writing/meta.rs
nodes.summary: Declares the new unplaceable-reference rule as house/comprehension and threads evidence through RuleMeta::resolve. Several example strings are reworded so they no longer trip the new rule.

nodes.label: Known names
nodes.subtitle: writing/names.rs
nodes.summary: Adds framework, standard and model names (React, Vite, RFC, Sonnet, Opus, Haiku) so a version number after them is not a candidate, and exposes is_generic_word so a generic label word never counts as a name.

nodes.label: resolve
nodes.subtitle: osf-lint-core meta.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves a finding's level and remediation from class, group, context, exception and now evidence. Statistical evidence short-circuits to warning plus advise before any other rule applies.

nodes.label: Skill finding resolution
nodes.subtitle: lints/skill.rs
nodes.summary: Passes each skill finding's evidence into the core resolver, so a statistical skill finding is advisory too.

nodes.label: Unplaceable fixture corpus
nodes.subtitle: tests/fixtures/writing/unplaceable
nodes.summary: 98 Markdown fixtures, each with an osf-unplaceable header naming its label, kind, target and reason. They cover numbers, phrases, times, names and model-only cases.

nodes.label: Precision/recall measure
nodes.subtitle: tests/unplaceable_measure.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the lint over every fixture, compares findings against each fixture's target, and requires 100% precision and recall per kind and in total, with no stray finding.

nodes.label: End-to-end checkpoints
nodes.subtitle: tests/unplaceable_checkpoints.rs
nodes.summary: Drives the compiled binary: a bare fix or issue number refuses the stop, a quoted label does not, a relative time passes in a reply but fails a commit message, and the prompt never names a retired rule id.

edges.label: candidate, paragraph

edges.label: known name lookup
edges.summary: The engine consults the known-names list to exclude a number after a real name and to skip a tool a project already knows.

edges.label: rule id, evidence

edges.label: class, group, context, evidence

edges.label: evidence
edges.summary: Skill findings now carry their evidence into the same resolver.

edges.label: fixture text
edges.summary: The measure lints every fixture in document context and scores the findings against each fixture's target.

edges.label: stop event on stdin
edges.summary: The checkpoint tests spawn the real binary and feed it a stop event.

edges.label: 98 labelled cases
edges.summary: Each fixture's header supplies the label, kind and target the measure scores against.
